content: Hi all :) @Fernando LEAL is an intern in my group, and @maxv is my PhD student supervising him, and together we'd like to help with Iris in Lean. :D Our general goal is to get an actual program logic on HeapLang working. I've already heard that there's other people here with the same goal so I am looking forward to working with everyone and I hope we can figure out a good way to partition the work. :)
Welcome! There's lots to do, let me know if you'd like help finding a first task. We do our best to keep the file PORTING.md up to date with the state of the port.

Markus de Medeiros said:

Sure! Right now I'm learning about Iris and how it's organized, but I'll be interested in tackling some "good first issues" to ensure I'm understanding things correctly. My current objective is to understand how iapply, and all concepts involved in its function, works

Hi Ralf!

I'm in the middle of finishing world satisfaction. There are still a few dangling sorry's + I'll need to refactor it, so I will most probably create a PR in a day or two.
I think some parts that could be possible to partition now are:

  • Fancy updates. I have not touched them yet (I think @Yunsong Yang works on them);
  • sbi_unfold. For the moment, when I need to provide BI wrappers of different algebras (e.g., gmap_view_both_validI_total), I just use long invocations of Si lemmas, but it would be nice to use sbi_unfold for that, when we need to port more of BI.
  • BI wrappers for algebras. I did a subset of gmap_view_* (HeapView in the Lean version) and agree_* wrappers required for wsat, but haven't touched anything else.

Sergei Stepanenko said:

  • Fancy updates. I have not touched them yet (I think @Yunsong Yang works on them);

To clarify, I think @Yunsong Yang is only working on supporting fancy updates in the proof mode, but not the model of fancy updates.
